candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — IV insulin preparation and monitoring
candidate.educational_objective: Prepare and monitor IV regular insulin according to the labeled concentration, diluent and safety-monitoring requirements.

options.A: Prepare the prescribed IV concentration in 0.9% sodium chloride and monitor blood glucose and potassium closely during the infusion.
options.B: Use the U-100 vial concentration directly in the IV line because dilution is required only for subcutaneous insulin administration.
options.C: Monitor blood glucose closely but omit potassium monitoring because intravenous regular insulin does not affect serum potassium.
options.D: Prepare the infusion in any concentration selected by the nurse because the label gives no concentration range for intravenous use.

candidate.rationale: HUMULIN R §2.2 permits IV administration only under medical supervision with close blood-glucose and potassium monitoring and specifies IV concentrations of 0.1 to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% sodium chloride. A follows these label requirements. B incorrectly uses the U-100 vial concentration directly, C omits potassium monitoring, and D ignores the labeled concentration range.
candidate.source_claim_supported: IV HUMULIN R requires prescribed dilution in 0.9% sodium chloride within the labeled concentration range and close glucose/potassium monitoring.
